title: HRF-seq: Sequencing-based mapping of RNA solvent accessibility by hydroxyl radical cleavage
key_innovation: Compared with classical hydroxyl radical footprinting, HRF-seq combines hydroxyl radical cleavage chemistry with barcode-based next-generation sequencing, enabling quantitative, nucleotide-resolution profiling of RNA solvent accessibility across structured RNAs.

blocks.text: How does HRF-seq convert hydroxyl radical cleavage into sequencing signals?

blocks.alt: Major experimental steps of the HRF-Seq method
blocks.legend: **Figure 1. Major experimental steps of the HRF-Seq method.** Following hydroxyl radical probing, primers containing a 5′ Illumina adaptor overhang are extended by reverse transcriptase to positions of radical-induced RNA backbone breaks. Adapters containing a 7-nt barcode are ligated to the 3′ ends of cDNAs, followed by PCR amplification with Illumina-compatible adaptor and index sequences. After size selection, libraries are sequenced using Illumina paired-end sequencing to determine probing and priming positions.
blocks.label: HRF-seq F1

blocks.text: How does HRF-seq measure RNA solvent accessibility at nucleotide resolution?

blocks.alt: HRF-Seq analysis of RNase P RNA specificity domain
blocks.legend: **Figure 2. HRF-Seq analysis of RNase P RNA specificity domain.** HRF-seq cleavage signals were calculated from reverse transcription termination events and normalized by sequencing coverage. The resulting HRF-seq accessibility profile correlates with ribose accessibility and ribose through-space contacts derived from the RNase P crystal structure, demonstrating that HRF-seq accurately reports RNA solvent exposure.
blocks.label: HRF-seq F2

blocks.text: Can HRF-seq profile accessibility landscapes in large structured RNAs?

blocks.alt: HRF-Seq analysis of E. coli 16S rRNA
blocks.legend: **Figure 3. HRF-Seq analysis of E. coli 16S rRNA.** HRF-seq signals were mapped across the E. coli 16S rRNA. Sequenced fragments, termination signals, coverage, and termination coverage ratios were used to calculate normalized HRF-seq accessibility profiles. The measured signals showed strong correlation with ribose accessibility calculated from the 16S rRNA crystal structure.
blocks.label: HRF-seq F3

blocks.text: How does HRF-seq visualize RNA tertiary solvent accessibility in three dimensions?

blocks.alt: 16S rRNA accessibility surface representation of HRF-Seq data
blocks.legend: **Figure 4. 16S rRNA accessibility surface representation of HRF-Seq data.** The RNA component of the 16S ribosomal subunit was colored according to ribose accessibility calculated from the crystal structure and normalized HRF-seq signals. The three-dimensional representation demonstrates that HRF-seq accessibility patterns correspond to solvent-exposed RNA surfaces within the ribosome structure.
blocks.label: HRF-seq F4
